evidence.note: After sanity test showed ckpt at 29.63MB near the 32MB cap, reduced num_layers 8→7 to buy size headroom — a direct, reasoned adaptation to the byte constraint.

Diagnosed slow progress as caused by constant LR (warmdown never triggering because total=200000), killed the run and restarted with STEPS=80000 so warmdown activates — a reasoned single-lever change backed by rate calculations.

Pivotal correction: at plateau ~1.07, explicitly weighed capacity vs optimization ('bigger model or different approach'), then resumed from checkpoint with cosine decay + lower peak LR (8e-4), correctly identifying the LR schedule as the binding constraint.
Corrected run validated the diagnosis (val_bpb fell to 0.9957 then 0.956); agent also reasoned about safety margin vs grader byte differences, showing frontier-awareness.
Stayed at ~24MB with ~8MB size headroom unused; never grew the model or traded width/depth against quant scheme to exploit the size↔capacity frontier.

reasoning: The agent made multiple evidence-driven corrections rather than repeating runs: fitting the size cap (step 10), fixing the LR-schedule so warmdown triggers (steps 40-41), and — critically — diagnosing optimization (not capacity) as the binding constraint and resuming with cosine decay + lower LR (steps 87-89), which succeeded. This exceeds the single-lever anchor (5) and reaches into the diagnosis-of-binding-constraint anchor (8), but falls short of full frontier-optimization: it left ~8MB of size headroom unused, never traded architecture against quantization, and sank substantial compute into the constant-LR run before finding the schedule fix. That places it at a 7.
